issue_context.title: [Flaky tests] NodeFeature:HugePage in ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting reports about failing tests in Kubernetes CI jobs -->

**Which jobs are failing**:
`ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial`

**Which test(s) are failing**:
`NodeFeature:HugePage`-tests

**Since when has it been failing**:
Unsure

**Testgrid link**:
https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-kubelet#node-kubelet-serial&include-filter-by-regex=Huge&show-stale-tests=

**Reason for failure**:
Unable to pre allocate 50x2MiB huge pages, probably due to memory pressure caused by kernel level caching. If requesting an substantial amount of huge page memory (like the tests), it is recommended to to it as early after boot as possible, or by using the kernel cmd line.

Eg. this one: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial/1159710677724565504

**Anything else we need to know**:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/79241 will fix this issue, but in awaiting for that, we can just decrease the page count in the tests.
comments: I think the reason of railure `50x2KiB huge pages` should be `50x2MiB huge pages` because a single hugepage of x86 is 2MiB as https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/vm/hugetlbpage.txt and a single page is 4KiB, not 2KiB.

> I think the reason of railure 50x2KiB huge pages should be 50x2MiB huge pages because a single hugepage of x86 is 2MiB as https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/vm/hugetlbpage.txt and a single page is 4KiB, not 2KiB.

Yes, `50x2MiB` is correct. Thanks for catching the typo :smile:

Looks like we still have some flakes in the huge page test, even tho the test now only requests `10MiB` of huge page memory. Happens way less frequently than previously tho.

```
_output/local/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/hugepages_test.go:178
Timed out after 30.000s.
Expected
    <*errors.errorString | 0xc001561580>: {
        s: "expected hugepages 5, but found 2",
    }
to be nil
_output/local/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/hugepages_test.go:191
```

This is probably because the kernel is caching a lot of stuff, making it hard for the kernel to fix it. Ill do some testing with dropping the caches (no user facing stuff will happen, only kernel level) before trying to pre allocate huge pages.

/reopen

review_comments: Nit: I may be missing something obvious, but how come this is `6Mi` instead of `5Mi`?

`5Mi` will work, but imo. it is a bit strange to say that we want 2.5 huge pages (since their size is 2Mi). k8s will not complain, same with the kernel. In reality you can then only use `4Mi`, since the kernel will floor the page count.

Yeah, we need to set multiplication of 2MiB which is a single hugepage on x86 architecture.
On the above, the test sets 10MiB(2MiB * 5) as hugepage.
In addition, the corresponding issue says the test could not allocated 100MiB hugepage but it was 84Mib(2MiB*42).
I guess 10MiB is not invalid here based on the failure case.
Anyways, I am fine for current change.
